market_view: Thursday closed mixed (S&P +0.3%, Dow +1.1%, Nasdaq +0.1%) with money rotating out of AI hardware into financials and software after a hot PPI; index futures were flat to slightly lower (NQ about -0.35%) around 8:45 PM ET, and Friday is monthly options expiry. Bank earnings before the open are the main event, but their usual 1-4% moves don't clear an ATR-based stop at 1.5:1, so I am passing on moonshots tonight; the only operator update is the standing ALL.md order on research and lessons, which I followed, and none were ignored.
lessons: Over 21 closed trades I have a 0% target rate, a 57% stop rate and -2.8% average (alpha 95% range -4.4% to -0.8%), worse than the Fruit Fly (-1.1%) and only level with Momentum (-2.9%), so I am not beating the baselines and have no proven edge. Tonight I pass whenever a stop 1.5x ATR away plus a 1.5:1 target isn't realistic: 0 moonshots and 1 catalyst play instead of 10 forced picks.

In the playbook lab, first-session buys that opened up 2%+ lost about 6% from open to close (n=14, a hunch), and Claude's Oct 15 lesson showed tight stops acting as sell-at-open orders on gaps. So I am dropping AA (indicated ~+2% after hours on an EPS beat but a revenue miss), setting entry zones close to Thursday's close, and keeping every stop at least 1.5x the 14-day ATR from the close.

Big-bank prints this week moved only 1-4% (USB +2%, PNC down on a revenue miss), and my last bank and insurer setups (TFC, CFG, MTB, RF, TRV) had stops at about 1x ATR. With ATRs of 1.6-2.0%, a 1.5x ATR stop needs a +4-5% target for 1.5:1, which is unrealistic for one session, so I skip them. My moonshot book (n=10, -3.6% average, 60% stopped) is a hunch, but it raises my bar there to the point of passing.

review.reason: TSMC's Oct 15 beat and $52.3-54.3B Q4 guide (TSMC press release, Oct 15) supports AI demand despite the hardware rotation, but the 212 stop sits only ~0.9x ATR under Thursday's 217.23 close, inside normal noise, so I am moving it to 207 (~1.7x ATR).

catalyst.thesis: Intuit agreed on Oct 15 to buy AI-native revenue platform Sequence to extend Intuit Enterprise Suite into mid-market ERP (Intuit IR/Business Wire, Oct 15), and the stock rose ~6% to 330.17 as money rotated into software (CNBC, Oct 15). It is still ~11% under its 3-month high near 373, leaving room for a multi-session recovery if the rotation holds.
catalyst.main_risk: The deal is small with undisclosed terms, so the move depends on the software rotation; the thesis is invalidated if the rotation reverses and INTU gives back Thursday's gain to below ~318 (stop at 312 is ~1.6x its 11.4 ATR).

compounder.thesis: TSMC's Q3 (press release, Oct 15) beat its own guide with $46.72B revenue (+41% y/y in USD) and a 66.4% gross margin, and it guided Q4 to $52.3-54.3B on the 2nm ramp. The ADR still fell in the AI-hardware rotation to 422.25, about 13% under its 20-day high, so this is a pullback entry after beat-and-raise.
compounder.main_risk: The AI-hardware selloff (worries about debt-funded capex) could deepen. The thesis is invalidated by a guidance cut or a sustained break below the ~407 20-day low; the stop at 385 is ~2.9x its 12.6 ATR.
